author: big sky times
title: Montana State University to honor largest Hilleman Scholars graduating class on April 27
text:
Montana State University will host a graduation and awards celebration on April 27 for the largest group of Hilleman Scholars to date, with 25 undergraduate students from Montana expected to graduate this spring. The event will take place in Inspiration Hall at Asbjornson Hall from 4 to 5 p.m. and is open to the public. Elizabeth Burroughs, head of the Department of Mathematical Sciences in MSU’s College of Letters and Science, will deliver the keynote address.
The ceremony highlights both student achievement and the university’s commitment as a land-grant institution focused on research, education, and community outreach. Carina Beck, director of the MSU Hilleman Scholars program and associate vice president of university initiatives, said: “We’re hosting an important rite of passage celebration for the Hilleman Scholar community. The students are representative of the public land-grant mission, and we also want to honor the legacy of Dr. Hilleman. We’re shaping the future, and these graduates represent the future of Montana.”
The MSU Hilleman Scholars Program supports Montana residents who show strong academic performance as well as leadership potential. Named after Maurice Hilleman—a Miles City native who graduated at the top of his class in 1941 before becoming a leading vaccinologist—the program was established in 2016 to invest in Montana’s future by educating its residents.
Hilleman Scholars are expected to graduate within four years while participating in mentoring programs, learning development activities, internships, and community service for up to ten hours per week throughout their scholarship period. Before starting their first year at MSU, scholars attend a Summer Success Academy focusing on math, writing, and critical thinking skills.
Montana State University leads research funding statewide with annual expenditures exceeding $288 million according to its official website. The university contributes through volunteer efforts as well as outreach programs designed to improve lives and protect natural resources according to its official website. It ranks among the top five percent globally per Center for World University Rankings according to its official website.
MSU enrolls about 17,165 students evenly divided between state residents and nonresidents according to its official website. As Montana’s land-grant institution focused on addressing key challenges through research and education according to its official website, it continues extending influence across communities within Montana—and beyond according to its official website.
